info.name: Idiot Pedals
info.description:
Idiot Pedals API — every mounted route, matching the code in server/src.

WARNING — REAL SIDE EFFECTS
- Register, a COD order (paymentMethod "cod") and Verify Payment send a REAL email unless the server runs with EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED=false. Start the API with that flag while testing: EMAIL_NOTIFICATIONS_ENABLED=false npm run dev
- Use Razorpay TEST keys only (rzp_test_...). Never point this collection at live keys.
- The "Setup (run once, manual)" folder creates the REAL storefront product (slug neon-fuzz-box). Run it by hand, never as part of an automated run. The other folders are automated: they create a product whose slug starts with "postman-temp-" and delete it at the end.

SETUP
- Fill in your Postman environment, including razorpayWebhookSecret, and select it before running anything.
- Login saves {{accessToken}}; create order saves {{orderId}} and {{orderNumber}}; create product saves {{productId}}; create payment saves {{razorpayOrderId}}.
- Endpoints marked (admin) need the token of an admin account.
- Register, Login and the order bodies contain PASTE_... placeholders: replace them with a test account you control. They are intentionally not variables, so no credential is stored in this file.
- Google OAuth returns 302: turn OFF "Automatically follow redirects" in Postman settings to see it.

request.description: SENDS A REAL EMAIL. The account exists only after the emailed link is opened. phone must be exactly 10 digits.
Token in the JSON body (never the URL): the POST consumes it. Distinct outcomes: 200 EMAIL_VERIFIED, 400 EMAIL_TOKEN_INVALID, 410 EMAIL_TOKEN_EXPIRED, 409 ACCOUNT_ALREADY_VERIFIED.
Always answers the same generic 200 body whether or not a pending registration exists (no existence oracle). Throttled per IP and per email address.
Returns data.accessToken and sets the httpOnly refresh cookie. Saves {{accessToken}}.
The session user. 401 without a valid token.
Uses the httpOnly refresh cookie (no body). Rotates the cookie and returns a new accessToken.
Clears the refresh cookie.
302 to Google. Browser flow; turn off automatic redirect following to see the 302.
Google calls this. Always 302: success -> FRONTEND_URL/auth/callback, failure -> FRONTEND_URL/login?error=<code>.
No Authorization header: 401.

item.name: Orders
item.description: Order creation and retrieval. Line items carry productId + quantity only.

request.description: The server prices the order from its own catalogue. paymentMethod "cod" SENDS A REAL EMAIL; "razorpay" does not. Saves {{orderId}} and {{orderNumber}}.

exec: // The client must never send a price: no price/amount anywhere, and each
// line item must be exactly { productId, quantity }.

request.description: Caller-scoped. limit is capped at 50.
Owner only. Accepts the internal ObjectId or the order number.
Same endpoint, addressed by the human-readable IP-... order number.
Owner only. Cancels a pending order and releases its stock reservation. Idempotent: an already-cancelled order returns 200. A paid/fulfilled order is rejected; another user's order is 404.
A valid ObjectId belonging to nobody. Another user's order must be 404, never 403 — a 403 would confirm it exists.

item.name: Payments
item.description: Razorpay order creation and verification. Test keys only.

request.description: Creates the Razorpay order for the server-computed paise total and saves {{razorpayOrderId}}. Idempotent per order: a second call returns the same Razorpay order.
SENDS A REAL EMAIL on a genuine confirmation. Confirms but never fulfils: the webhook finalizes. Replay-safe and idempotent.

item.name: NEGATIVE — verify with a bad signature

request.description: A forged signature is rejected before any provider call.

item.name: NEGATIVE — create payment for someone else's order

request.description: An order that is not the caller's: 404.

item.name: Webhooks
item.description: Razorpay calls these server-to-server. The frontend never does.

request.description: The only path that finalizes an order (fulfilled) and consumes the stock reservation. The signature must cover the exact raw bytes, which is why the pre-request script signs pm.request.body.raw.

exec: if (!secret) { throw new Error('razorpayWebhookSecret is missing from the active Postman environment.'); }
// CryptoJS ships with the Postman sandbox.

item.name: NEGATIVE — webhook with a bad signature

request.description: Only a bad signature is a 4xx; duplicate and already-processed events still return 200.
